Express the terms inside the parentheses in terms of $\sin\theta$ and $\cos\theta$:
$$\frac{1}{\cos\theta} - \tan\theta = \frac{1}{\cos\theta} - \frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \frac{1 - \sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$$

Square the quotient and apply the identity $\cos^2\theta = 1 - \sin^2\theta$:
$$\left(\frac{1 - \sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\right)^2 = \frac{(1 - \sin\theta)^2}{\cos^2\theta} = \frac{(1 - \sin\theta)^2}{1 - \sin^2\theta}$$

Factorise the difference of two squares in the denominator and cancel the common factor $(1 - \sin\theta)$:
$$\frac{(1 - \sin\theta)^2}{(1 - \sin\theta)(1 + \sin\theta)} = \frac{1 - \sin\theta}{1 + \sin\theta} = \text{RHS}$$

Use the proven identity from part (i) to simplify the equation:
$$\frac{1 - \sin\theta}{1 + \sin\theta} = \frac{1}{2}$$

Find the solutions for $\theta$ in the range $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$:
$$\theta_1 = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \approx 19.47^\circ \approx 19.5^\circ$$
$$\theta_2 = 180^\circ - 19.47^\circ \approx 160.53^\circ \approx 160.5^\circ$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } \theta = 19.5^\circ, \quad 160.5^\circ)$$
